SELECT metric, service_name, count(*) n, avg(value) avgv, max(value) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name IN ('ts-order-other-service','mysql','ts-preserve-service','ts-seat-service') AND (metric LIKE '%db%' OR metric LIKE '%connection%' OR metric LIKE '%cpu%' OR metric LIKE '%memory%') GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 2,1 LIMIT 60

content.text: Order-other-service logs show HikariPool timeouts and MySQL communication failures, while mysql's own CPU and memory look normal. Next I'll look at order-other-service's own metrics and its network connection to mysql.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, metric, service_name, count(*) n, round(avg(value),3) avgv, round(max(value),3) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics WHERE service_name = 'ts-order-other-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'abn_sum', metric, service_name, count(*), round(avg(value),3), round(max(value),3) FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE service_name = 'ts-order-other-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, service_name, count(*), round(avg(value),3), round(max(value),3) FROM normal_metrics WHERE service_name = 'ts-order-other-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3 ORDER BY 2,1 LIMIT 120

SELECT 'abn' p, metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avgv, round(max(value),2) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE attr_source LIKE '%order-other%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%order-other%' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE attr_source LIKE '%order-other%' OR attr_destination LIKE '%order-other%' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,1 LIMIT 80

content.text: Network drops around order-other-service are flat, so the database failure is not showing as packet loss. Next I'll compare its database spans over time and check which services call mysql.

input.query: SELECT 'abn' p, service_name, span_name, attr_status_code, count(*) n, round(approx_quantile(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50ms, round(approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95ms FROM abnormal_traces WHERE span_name IN ('SELECT Order') OR service_name='ts-order-other-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', service_name, span_name, attr_status_code, count(*), round(approx_quantile(duration,0.5)/1e6,1), round(approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) FROM normal_traces WHERE span_name IN ('SELECT Order') OR service_name='ts-order-other-service' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 1,3,4 LIMIT 80

SELECT 'abn' p, metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*) n, round(avg(value),2) avgv, round(max(value),2) maxv FROM abnormal_metrics_sum WHERE attr_destination LIKE '%mysql%' OR attr_source LIKE '%mysql%' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 UNION ALL SELECT 'norm', metric, attr_source, attr_destination, count(*), round(avg(value),2), round(max(value),2) FROM normal_metrics_sum WHERE attr_destination LIKE '%mysql%' OR attr_source LIKE '%mysql%' GROUP BY 1,2,3,4 ORDER BY 2,1 LIMIT 80

content.text: Order-other-service is clearly failing its own database calls. Next I'll check whether any other service started failing independently, by finding the earliest error span per service.

input.query: WITH t0 AS (SELECT min(time) m FROM abnormal_traces) SELECT service_name, count(*) total, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, round(min(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN epoch(time - t0.m) END),1) first_err_s, round(min(epoch(time - t0.m)),1) first_span_s, round(max(epoch(time - t0.m)),1) last_span_s, round(approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95ms FROM abnormal_traces, t0 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY first_err_s NULLS LAST

WITH t0 AS (SELECT min(time) m FROM normal_traces) SELECT service_name, count(*) total, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, round(approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95ms, round(max(epoch(time - t0.m)),1) last_span_s FROM normal_traces, t0 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY errs DESC

content.text: The error cascade starts at ts-order-other-service at about 0.2 s and spreads upward through security, seat, travel2, and the planners. Next I'll check whether the later food-service and consign-service shifts (onset 62 s and 192 s) are separate faults.

input.query: WITH t0 AS (SELECT min(time) m FROM abnormal_traces) SELECT service_name, CAST(floor(epoch(time - t0.m)/30) AS INT)*30 bucket_s, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) errs, round(approx_quantile(duration,0.5)/1e6,1) p50ms, round(approx_quantile(duration,0.95)/1e6,1) p95ms FROM abnormal_traces, t0 WHERE service_name IN ('ts-food-service','ts-station-food-service','ts-train-food-service','ts-consign-service','ts-consign-price-service') AND attr_span_kind='SERVER' GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 1,2

content.text: The food and consign shifts come from low traffic in the abnormal window, not separate faults: those services have almost no abnormal spans. Next I'll confirm the call edges by joining parent and child spans.

input.query: SELECT c.service_name AS callee, p.service_name AS caller, count(*) n, sum(CASE WHEN c.attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) callee_err, sum(CASE WHEN p.attr_status_code='Error' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) caller_err, round(approx_quantile(c.duration,0.5)/1e6,1) callee_p50ms FROM abnormal_traces c JOIN abnormal_traces p ON c.trace_id=p.trace_id AND c.parent_span_id=p.span_id WHERE c.service_name<>p.service_name GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY caller_err DESC, n DESC LIMIT 40
